samples.summary: Cursor.position now always materializes a lineAffinity, which defeats the out-of-diff "selection start defaults to forward" rule wherever a shift-selection anchor falls back to the caret
samples.evidence: `buildRects` (packages/docs/src/view/selection.ts:260-261) relies on an *absent* affinity to apply the asymmetric default: `const startAffinity = start.lineAffinity ?? 'forward'`. Before this change a keyboard-derived caret position carried no `lineAffinity` (Cursor.moveTo stored `pos` verbatim and kept the affinity in a sibling field), so anchors built from the caret hit that default. After the change `cursor.position` always has one (cursor.ts:26/39/55). The anchor fallbacks are all out of the diff: packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:2774 (`const anchor = this.selection.range?.anchor ?? pos`), :2807 (shift+Home), :2826 (shift+End), :2841, :2857 — each now hands `buildRects` a start endpoint carrying the caret's reading (typically `'backward'` after typing or ArrowLeft, `'forward'` after ArrowRight). `getNormalizedRange` returns endpoints as stored (selection.ts:705), so a shift-selection begun at a wrap boundary now paints its first rect on the previous visual line / as a zero-width sliver — exactly the artefact the comment at selection.ts:255-259 says the default exists to prevent. The same normalized endpoints are published to presence, so peers see it too. Fix likely belongs on the new code (do not materialize `'backward'` on carets that never chose one, or make the anchor fallback drop the caret's affinity).

samples.summary: `moveTo`'s default changed from a hard 'backward' to "inherit pos.lineAffinity"; several out-of-diff callers pass positions that already carry an affinity and previously relied on the reset
samples.evidence: `Cursor.moveTo(pos)` used to force `'backward'` when no affinity argument was given (old signature `affinity: 'forward' | 'backward' = 'backward'`); it now inherits `pos.lineAffinity`. Callers that pass selection endpoints or resolved positions therefore change behaviour without being touched: packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:2789 (`this.cursor.moveTo(collapsePos)` — collapsing a selection with ArrowLeft/Up now adopts the *start* endpoint's `'forward'` reading, drawing the caret at the start of the next visual line instead of the end of the previous one), :3384 and :3449 (`this.cursor.moveTo(start)` after deleting a selection), :1569 / :1580 / :1617 (`this.cursor.moveTo(focus)` on click/drag paths), and packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:3689 (`_setSelectionForTest` now inherits the focus reading). None of these were reviewed against the new default.

samples.summary: The sibling text-box editor's onCursorMove contract was left at the narrow `{blockId, offset}` shape while the docs editor widened to DocPosition, and its de-dupe key silently changed meaning
samples.evidence: packages/docs/src/view/text-box-editor.ts:329, :484 and :1289 still type the callback as `(pos: { blockId: string; offset: number }, …)` even though it is handed `cursor.position` (text-box-editor.ts:617, :648), which now always carries `lineAffinity` — so the slides consumer at packages/slides/src/view/editor/editor.ts:4224-4227 (`let cursorPos: { blockId: string; offset: number } | null`) receives a field its type denies, and the JSON de-dupe keys at text-box-editor.ts:614/647 now differ on affinity-only moves, firing extra cursor-move notifications that previously coalesced. Behaviour is still correct, but the type/comment now describe the old contract.

samples.summary: Peer-cursor change detection keys on blockId:offset only, so an affinity-only peer caret move no longer counts as a move now that affinity is rendered
samples.evidence: packages/frontend/src/app/docs/docs-view.tsx:283 builds `posKey = `${activeCursorPos.blockId}:${activeCursorPos.offset}`` and uses it to decide whether to re-show the peer's name label. Now that `lineAffinity` is published on every caret and honoured when drawing the peer caret (packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:1570), a peer whose caret visibly jumps between the two visual lines of a wrap boundary produces an unchanged `posKey` and gets no label re-show. `setPeerCursors` at line 314 still runs, so the caret itself redraws.

verdict.reason: All claimed code is present and reachable. Cursor.position now always materializes a lineAffinity (cursor.ts:26, 38-40, 52-57, documented at cursor.ts:12-19), while the out-of-diff consumer buildRects applies its asymmetric "start defaults to forward" rule only when the endpoint carries no affinity (selection.ts:260-261, with the rationale comment at 255-259). Nothing on the path strips it: normalizeRange returns endpoints verbatim (selection.ts:124-125, 166-168, 178-180) and Selection.setRange/getNormalizedRange explicitly keep them as stored (selection.ts:685-713). The anchor fallbacks that now hand a caret-derived affinity into that start endpoint are out of the diff and reachable: text-editor.ts:2455 feeds 2774, plus 2807, 2826, 2841, 2857 (and 1572, 1620, 2719). Keyboard carets really do sit at 'backward' (text-editor.ts:2770; test/view/caret-line-affinity.test.ts:155-161), and the repo's own test documents the resulting artefact: a backward-affinity start opens the highlight on the previous visual line (test/view/selection-line-affinity.test.ts:104-115) instead of the single rect an affinity-less start produces (:117-125). Impact is zero-width in body text (selection.ts:503-509) but a visible tail to the cell edge in the cell-internal branch (selection.ts:427-429), and the same endpoints are published to peers (view/editor.ts:1990; frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:1059) and re-rendered via computeSelectionRects (selection.ts:547). No guard, no not-present element, and it is in-lane for blast radius (behaviour change to a shared symbol whose other consumers were not updated), so I cannot refute it.
